transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Well, I came in because... I'm having this issue with eating. Once I start eating, it feels like I just disappear. It's like something else takes over, and even while I'm in my head telling myself to stop, I can't. I just keep going and going until I physically can't stand it anymore.
After these episodes where you can't stop eating, do you do anything to try to undo or compensate for what you've eaten, such as making yourself vomit, using laxatives, or exercising excessively?

Yeah, I do. After I eat like that, I usually end up in a bathroom in my dorm, or sometimes I'll go up to a quiet floor of the library. I make myself throw up. I just... I get this terrified feeling that all that food is just sitting inside me, turning into weight. So I have to get it out.

latest_inference.note: Patient describes binge eating followed by purging (self-induced vomiting), which is pathognomonic for Bulimia Nervosa (F50.2). F50.81 (binge eating disorder) ruled out due to purging behavior. F63.2 (trichotillomania) and F91.9 (conduct disorder) are not relevant to eating disorder presentation.

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient presents with recurrent binge eating episodes (loss of control, consuming large quantities until physical discomfort) followed by regular compensatory purging behavior (self-induced vomiting). This clinical presentation is diagnostic of Bulimia Nervosa (F50.2). The patient demonstrates the core diagnostic features: binge-eating/purging cycle with associated anxiety about weight gain and body image concerns.

confirmed_symptoms: Loss of control during eating ('feels like I just disappear', 'something else takes over')
Inability to stop eating despite internal resistance ('even while I'm in my head telling myself to stop, I can't')
Continued eating until physical discomfort ('until I physically can't stand it anymore')
Regular self-induced vomiting after binge episodes
Purposeful use of purging to prevent weight gain ('I get this terrified feeling that all that food is just sitting inside me, turning into weight. So I have to get it out')
Fear of weight gain associated with food consumption
Anxiety about food remaining in the body and converting to weight

additional_requirements: Binge-eating and purging occurring regularly as part of established pattern
